node: Tariff-sheltered domestic materials and strategic industrial inputs
summary: Expanded the universe around scarce domestic materials and strategic industrial inputs where tariffs, Buy America-style procurement, defense qualification, or domestic-content rules can redirect demand to a thin U.S. supplier base. The strongest chokepoint evidence in this pass is NewMarket via AMPAC ammonium perchlorate, where a single domestic facility and requalification friction create a clear policy/defense supply-chain bottleneck. MP Materials and Energy Fuels are critical-minerals candidates tied to rare earth/magnet supply security; they are more visible than the ideal underfollowed profile but still map directly to regulated domestic-content and foreign-dependency concerns. Century Aluminum is included as a tariff-sheltered industrial-input reference/discovery hybrid because Section 232 aluminum policy directly affects U.S. primary aluminum capacity, though the commodity nature makes the bottleneck less clean than specialty chemicals or qualified defense inputs.
